prompt: A real news-agency style night photograph made with a long telephoto lens from across the Thames: the clock tower and the nearest stretch of the Palace of Westminster's riverfront fill most of the picture, compressed and flat the way a long lens flattens distance. It is pouring: diagonal rain streaks cross the whole picture and a grey haze of spray sits between us and the stone, so the building's detail is soft and its floodlit stone a dull honey colour rather than gold. The clock face glows a plain cool white. Above, a heavy overcast lit a dirty orange-brown by the city below. The darker water at the very bottom edge, ruffled by wind. Slightly underexposed, visible high-ISO grain and a little noise in the shadows, colours muted and a touch green, the focus not quite perfect. An honest, ordinary picture, nothing heroic about it. Nobody in shot, no boats, no flags, no signage, no writing.
